dmp.title: NeuroConsent Data Management Plan
dmp.description: Worked example: personal and sensitive data under controlled access. All content is synthetic; the DOIs use DataCite's test prefix 10.5072 and resolve nowhere.
dmp.ethical_issues_description: Human participants; approval by the institutional ethics committee is required before data collection.

dataset.title: Behavioural study responses
dataset.description: Pseudonymised responses of about 400 participants to a behavioural task.

security_and_privacy.title: Pseudonymisation
security_and_privacy.description: Direct identifiers are removed; the linking key is held separately under restricted access.

security_and_privacy.title: Access control and encryption
security_and_privacy.description: Encrypted storage, role-based access, oversight by the data protection officer.

dataset.preservation_statement: Kept for ten years, then reviewed for deletion under the terms of the consent.

distribution.title: Behavioural study responses (controlled access)
distribution.description: Available to researchers on request under a data-sharing agreement.

guide.title: Practical Guide to the International Alignment of Research Data Management

answers.1a: New data are collected from participants through an online behavioural task; no existing data are re-used.
answers.1b: Tabular responses in CSV, about 200 MB, and a codebook in PDF.
answers.2a: A codebook defines every variable and its units; the deposit carries DataCite metadata and a README.
answers.2b: Responses are validated on entry against the task's allowed ranges, and a second person checks a 10% sample.
answers.3a: During the project the data are kept on the institution's encrypted research storage, backed up nightly to a second site.
answers.3b: Only the three researchers named in the ethics approval have access. The linking key between participants and pseudonyms is kept apart from the data.
answers.4a: Processing rests on informed consent under the GDPR. Data are pseudonymised at collection, and the data protection officer reviews the processing record yearly.
answers.4b: The data are owned by the project's institution. They are shared under CC BY-NC 4.0, only with researchers who sign the data-sharing agreement.
answers.4c: The study is reviewed by the institutional ethics committee before any data are collected, and follows the national code of conduct for research integrity.
answers.5a: The pseudonymised responses are deposited at the end of the project with controlled access: researchers apply, and access is granted under a data-sharing agreement.
answers.5b: Only the pseudonymised responses and the codebook are kept; the linking key is destroyed at the end of the project. They go to a CoreTrustSeal-certified repository with controlled access.
answers.5d: The repository assigns a DOI to the deposit, reserved in advance and recorded in this plan.
answers.6a: The principal investigator is responsible for the plan; the data steward carries it out, and the data protection officer oversees the personal data.
answers.6b: EUR 3,500 for secure storage and the controlled-access repository, and about a month of the data steward's time.
